summary: In this episode, Fr. Andrew and Fr. Stephen discuss the Orthodox concept of theosis (deification) as the true understanding of salvation, contrasting it with Western individualistic and forensic models. They argue that salvation is not merely about satisfying divine justice or personal improvement, but about humanity's original purpose: to become like God and join the angelic hosts as 'sons of God.' The hosts trace this theme from God's promises to Abraham (that his offspring would be 'as the stars') through St. Paul's writings, showing that theosis is the plan from creation, not a later addition. They also address questions about demons and mental illness, the loss of this teaching in the West, and the difference between sanctification and theosis.

entities.title: Fr. Andrew Stephen Damick

entities.title: Fr. Stephen De Young
entities.summary: Orthodox priest and co-host, biblical scholar, based in Lafayette, Louisiana.

entities.title: Abraham
entities.summary: Patriarch to whom God made promises about his offspring becoming as the stars.

entities.title: St. Paul
entities.summary: Apostle and writer of many New Testament epistles; his writings are reinterpreted in light of theosis.

entities.title: St. Athanasius of Alexandria
entities.summary: Church Father known for his teaching on theosis and the incarnation.

entities.title: Philo of Alexandria
entities.summary: First-century Jewish philosopher who wrote about the stars as divine beings.

concepts.title: Theosis (Deification)
concepts.summary: The Orthodox understanding of salvation as becoming partakers of the divine nature, being adopted as sons of God, and joining the angelic hosts in governing creation.

concepts.title: Sons of God
concepts.summary: A term referring to angelic beings in the Old Testament, and also to humans who are adopted through Christ and become equal to the angels, sharing in divine governance.

concepts.title: Promises to Abraham
concepts.summary: God's promises that Abraham's offspring would be as the stars of heaven, indicating they would become like the angelic hosts who govern creation.

concepts.title: Adoption as Sons (Huiothesia)
concepts.summary: The concept of being made sons of God through Christ, which is central to theosis and involves receiving the Spirit and becoming heirs of God.

claims.text: Salvation is not merely about satisfying divine justice or individual improvement, but about becoming like God and joining the angelic hosts as sons of God.
God's promise that Abraham's offspring would be 'as the stars' means they would become like the angelic beings who govern creation.
St. Paul should be understood as a prophet and mystic, not a modern theologian, which changes how we read his writings on salvation.
Sanctification and theosis are not separate processes; they are facets of the same reality of being conformed to Christ.

scriptural_links.summary: God tells Abram his offspring will be as the stars.
God promises to multiply Abraham's offspring as the stars and sand, and that his seed will possess the gate of his enemies.
God reiterates the promise to Abraham about offspring as the stars and blessing all nations.
When the Most High divided the nations, he fixed their boundaries according to the number of the sons of God.
Jesus says the sons of the resurrection are equal to the angels and are sons of God.
Through baptism, believers are sons of God and Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise.
Believers receive adoption as sons and are heirs through God.
Those led by the Spirit are sons of God, heirs with Christ.
Creation waits for the revealing of the sons of God and the redemption of our bodies.
God predestined us to be conformed to the image of his Son.

glossary.definition: The process of becoming like God, deification, or divinization; the Orthodox understanding of salvation.
Greek term for adoption as sons, used in the context of becoming sons of God.
A term for angelic beings in the Old Testament, and for humans adopted through Christ.
